records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] embed.js reads the globals discourseUrl and discourseEmbedUrl with no guard, and the iframe is created with no initial height, so any embedding page that fails to define both globals exactly gets a broken or invisible comment box. A publisher who copies the JS but names the variable discourseURL or sets it after the script runs gets an immediate ReferenceError and no comments render at all; even on the happy path the iframe has no height until the first postMessage arrives, so pages flash a zero-height box or clip content when the resize message is lost (e.g. the reload-referer case above).
records.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the script directly reads `discourseUrl` and `discourseEmbedUrl` as free globals (`iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + encodeURIComponent(discourseEmbedUrl);`). If either global is not defined when this runs, it will throw a `ReferenceError` and the embed will fail to render. Also the iframe is appended without any initial `height` being set (only `width`, `frameBorder`, and `scrolling` are set), and scrolling is disabled (`iframe.scrolling = "no"`), so content can be clipped until/if a resize postMessage arrives.

Any attacker can curl /embed/best?embed_url=... with a forged Referer to bypass the host gate; impact is currently limited to triggering RetrieveTopic jobs (throttled to once/60s per URL per non-staff user) and viewing public topic content, but the control is security theater and downstream code treats it as an authorization decision.
records.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and raising on mismatch. This relies on the `Referer` header (client-controlled) as an authorization decision, so a non-browser client can trivially spoof it to pass the check and hit `/embed/best` (triggering `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` when no topic exists). records.issue_text: [BUG] The rss.items loop has no per-item or per-feed error handling, so a single malformed item aborts the entire poll mid-loop with no log and no error surfaced. If any item's i.content is nil (valid in RSS/Atom) `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError, or if any item's link/id resolution fails, the job dies after importing a prefix of the feed: the remaining items are silently skipped while the already-imported ones look successful, and sidekiq_options retry: false means nothing retries or reports until the next hourly run, which fails the same way — a persistent silent partial import.
records.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is `nil` (common for RSS items that only have `description`/`summary`), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError` and abort the job mid-iteration. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single bad item can stop further imports without automatic retry.

records.issue_text: [BUG] SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) performs an outbound HTTP fetch with no timeout. A slow or hung feed host blocks the Sidekiq worker thread indefinitely; with retry: false the poll is not retried, and because TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve invokes this same poll synchronously inside a RetrieveTopic job, one hung feed also wedges the embed-retrieval job and the user's iframe stays on the loading page with no timeout ever firing.
records.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed is fetched via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (Ruby `open-uri`) with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, so a slow/hung remote host can block the Sidekiq thread indefinitely. This is compounded by `sidekiq_options retry: false` in `Jobs::PollFeed`, and by `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously before falling back to HTTP retrieval, meaning a hung feed poll can also wedge the embed retrieval path initiated by `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`.
